A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeDelayed framework and retain corresponding main experiments, equations, and figures. All supplied pages, including both appendices, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original BDD100K segmentation experiments, including comparisons across inference configurations and delays in Figure 7 and Table 3.

after.justification: V3 retains those experiments and reports additional original ablation, robustness, runtime, and Nymeria evaluation results in its appendix.

M1.justification: The architecture, fusion operation, and training objective remain unchanged. Appendix 8.3 newly proposes an optional inference rule that selects received remote features using a precomputed accuracy matrix indexed by observed and conditioning delays; the PDFs do not establish that reported experiments use this rule.

E1.justification: V3 adds Nymeria egocentric semantic segmentation using the ADE20K taxonomy, including evaluation on unseen environments and actions, beyond the retained driving-scene coverage. It also explicitly evaluates mismatched delays and delays beyond the training range in Appendix 8.3.

E2.justification: The main comparison configurations in Figure 7 and Table 3 are retained. V3 Table 4 adds a delay-unconditioned variant as a controlled comparator against the full fused model; no new external competing method is evaluated.

E3.justification: The main experimental settings remain unchanged, but v3 documents substantial protocols for added experiments: a 0–10-frame delay-mismatch sweep, ten-epoch finetuning at 224/320/480-pixel local resolutions, and H.264/H.265 tests at 1/3/5 Mbps. Nymeria introduces training on 35k clips from 229 sequences and evaluation on 2k clips from 25 disjoint sequences.

E4.justification: V3 supplies the delay-mismatch heatmap absent behind v2's unresolved jitter reference. Appendices 8.4–8.10 additionally test local resolution, removal of delay conditioning, compression robustness, component costs, an unocclusion example, and validation pseudolabel quality.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional appendix results do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation; averaging the delay-ablation effect across conditions is not repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The existing Figure 7 and Table 3 results are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial numerical and qualitative evidence. Table 4 reports an average 0.015 mIoU decrease without delay conditioning; Table 7 reports Nymeria scores of 0.2450 at zero delay and 0.2443 at five frames versus 0.2034 locally. Compression, runtime, resolution, and mismatch results are newly reported under their respective settings.

T1.justification: The framework equations, notation, and task-loss formulation are retained. V3 adds implementation descriptions and empirical analyses, without new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The three stated contributions and central claims about delay-conditioned remote prediction, local fusion, and real-time applicability remain the same. The abstract retains the reported 100-ms improvements of 6.4 and 9.8 mIoU points; its added resource-release statement primarily changes reproducibility information.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of delay-mismatch robustness, explaining why underestimating delay can produce overconfident localization and recommending conservative delay inputs under jitter. It also discusses abrupt scene changes and specific pseudolabel ambiguities and boundary errors, while retaining the original interpretation of stale predictions and local fallback.

D1.justification: V2 provides an inline code sketch; v3 additionally announces training-code, pretrained-model, and library release with an access address. Its appendix clarifies tensor handling, delay-embedding layer sizes, and 3D block internals, and supplies codec settings, additional training details, and hardware/precision information for runtime measurements. Resource availability is asserted by the PDF, not externally verified.

R1.justification: V3 adds the Nymeria dataset paper as reference 28 for its new evaluation. The existing related-work categories, cited competing approaches, and positioning relative to prior research otherwise remain unchanged after matching renumbered references.

P1.justification: V3 standardizes the name to DeDelayed, makes localized wording edits, reorders the local and remote implementation descriptions, and places the expanded appendix after the references. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Figures 8–12 and Tables 4–7, including a heatmap, resolution curves, quantitative summaries, and qualitative examples. It also revises labels and styling in existing diagrams, particularly Figures 2, 3, 5, and 6, and reformats the full-page code listing into an appendix column.

improvement.justification: V2's practical robustness evidence centered on fixed-delay BDD100K results and included an unresolved reference to missing jitter evidence. V3 supplies that evidence, directly tests delay conditioning and compression, and adds a distinct evaluation domain, component runtimes, and substantial reproducibility information. These additions materially strengthen validation of the central deployment claims, although statistical uncertainty remains unreported.
